McCollum, D.L. and Ogden, J.M. (2006). Techno-Economic Models for Carbon Dioxide Compression, Transport, and Storage & Correlations for Estimating Carbon Dioxide Density and Viscosity. Research Report UCD-ITS-RR-06-14, Institute of Transportation Studies, University of California, Davis, October 2006. https://escholarship.org/uc/item/1zg00532

Report number UCD-ITS-RR-06-14 verified on the cover; first author McCollum, 2006. Three sections with separate printed page numbering; locators give section page and PDF page (Section I printed page = PDF page - 6). Loaded: CO2 compression (0.1 to 15 MPa, compressor plus pump) at seven flow rates from the printed labels of Fig. 4: capex derived as levelized capital / CRF 0.15 (per t delivered per year at CF 0.8), O&M per t, levelized total, and power 104.8 kWh/t (6.81 $/t / 0.065 $/kWh). Pipeline and storage: the report gives correlations, not point results, so only the O&M factor, site-screening capital, per-well O&M constants, CF and economic bases are in the main file; the correlations (pipeline 9970 m^0.35 L^0.13 $/km, drilling, injection equipment, compressor and pump capital) are in other-values for the coordinator. Not loaded: Section III appendix tables (replications of Ogden, MIT, Ecofys, IEA GHG models: reprinted models, not this report's results); Section II CO2 property correlations. All costs 2005 USD.
